What does NAND stand for?: How many transistors does a two-input NAND gate use in CMOS?
Four: two PMOS in parallel at the top, two NMOS in series at the bottom.

What does NAND stand for?: How many transistors does a two-input NOR gate use in CMOS?
Four — the same count as NAND, but with series and parallel positions swapped.

What does NAND stand for?: Why does NAND switch faster than NOR?
NAND uses NMOS transistors in series for its pull-down; electrons in NMOS are roughly twice as mobile as holes in PMOS, which NOR uses in series for its pull-up.
Every possible boolean function — any truth table, any number of inputs — can be built from NAND gates alone.

What does NAND stand for?: How do you build a NOT gate from a NAND gate?
Tie both inputs of a two-input NAND together.

What does NAND stand for?: Who proved that boolean algebra is the natural mathematics for switching circuits?
Claude Shannon, in his 1937 master’s thesis.

What does NAND stand for?: When does a CMOS gate consume power?
Only when it switches — when transistor capacitances are charged or discharged. Idle transistors are essentially free.

What does NAND stand for?: How many NAND gates does a full adder require?
Nine NAND gates per full adder.

What does NAND stand for?: Roughly how many gates does a frontier GPU contain?
On the order of 10<sup>11</sup> — about a hundred billion gates.
